lines.vo: Your messy desk may be quietly fighting your brain for attention.
That's not weak focus. That's too much stuff in view.
So before planning her week, Tasha clears the desk and opens her Life Reset Planner.
Princeton neuroscientists scanned people's brains while they looked at cluttered and simple displays.
Every object in view competes for a slice of your visual brain's attention.
With more clutter, the brain had a harder time focusing on any one thing.
Fewer things in view means less competition, so one task can win.
Clear the desk, pick one task, start. That's how you stay on track.

hook: Your messy desk is *fighting* your focus
